name: Macrogol 3350
route_note: Powder dissolved in water once daily for constipation; large-volume electrolyte solutions for bowel preparation
targets: None (osmotic action in the gut lumen)

discovery.by: Gordon Davis, John Fordtran and colleagues (Dallas)
discovery.note: Developed a non-absorbable polyethylene glycol–electrolyte lavage solution that cleanses the colon without net fluid or salt shifts.

rx_status: OTC (laxative); bowel-preparation kits prescription in many countries
tagline: Osmotic polymer laxative and basis of most bowel-preparation solutions
summary: Macrogol 3350 is a polyethylene glycol of average molecular weight 3350 that is not absorbed or metabolised. It holds water in the bowel by osmosis, softening stool, and in large volumes with electrolytes is used to clear the colon before colonoscopy.
mechanism: Macrogol molecules form hydrogen bonds with water and remain in the intestinal lumen, increasing stool water content and volume. Larger, softer stools stimulate colonic motility.
Because it is not fermented by colonic bacteria, it causes less gas than lactulose. Electrolytes in lavage and some laxative formulations prevent net sodium and water loss.
uses: Chronic and occasional constipation in adults and children
Bowel cleansing before colonoscopy or surgery (with electrolytes)

history.title: Lavage solution
history.detail: Davis and colleagues describe a PEG–electrolyte lavage solution for colon cleansing.

history.title: Bowel preparation
history.detail: FDA approves GoLYTELY for bowel cleansing.

history.title: Movicol
history.detail: Norgine launches Movicol, a macrogol–electrolyte laxative, in the UK.

history.title: MiraLAX
history.detail: FDA approves MiraLAX (prescription) for occasional constipation.

history.title: OTC switch
history.detail: MiraLAX becomes available over the counter in the US.

serious: Fluid and electrolyte disturbance with bowel-prep volumes
Aspiration in patients with impaired swallowing
Bowel perforation if obstruction is present

facts: Polyethylene glycols are also used as excipients and to PEGylate proteins such as pegfilgrastim.
The number 3350 refers to the polymer's average molecular weight.
